newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TISCO chief sees spate of mergers.
newsitem.headline: India's TISCO chief sees spate of mergers.

text.p: The head of India's premier business house said on Friday that domestic industry was ripe for a wave of mergers and acquisitions, but warned of "bloodshed" from the closure of non-competitive companies.
"Mergers and acquisitions have just started," Jamshed Irani, managing director of the Tata Iron and Steel Company Ltd (TISCO) told a group of businessmen.
"The last five years have been a period of awakening. The real bloodshed is yet to come," he said.
Irani, addressing a seminar on mergers and acquisitions, said sheer inertia had carried many inefficient Indian firms through the turbulent waters of economic reform.
But that period had now ended.
"Quite a few poor, out-of-date, non-competitive companies still survive," he said. "But not for much longer."
Indian economic reforms started in 1991, tearing down a decades-old socialist command economy and revitalising Indian industrialists with a new spirit of enterprise.
Recent major Indian mergers or acquisitions include detergent-maker Hindustan Lever Ltd's purchase of the Tata Oil Mills Company.
